tiles.name: Wall
tiles.explanation:
A castle wall for a background: dark stone with a few lit bricks picked out. The dark color fills most of the tile, and that is the point. A background should stay quiet so the characters in front of it read clearly.

Each brick is a pale block with darker red corners, which rounds it off without an outline.

![One tile, repeated](examples/one-repeated.png)

Repeated on its own, the bricks form the same group every 16 pixels.

tiles.name: Wall, second variant
tiles.explanation: A second tile with the bricks in other places. It shares the background and the colors with the first, so the two can sit side by side in any order.

tiles.name: Wall, third variant
tiles.explanation:
With a third tile you can mix all three so no pattern shows. Three plain variants are usually enough to hide the grid on a large background.

![The three tiles mixed](examples/mixed.png)
